summary.executeNext: Resolve the Control Plane experiment's deployment-scope blocker, then collect prospective run lineage before generalizing instrumentation. In parallel, continue read-only selected-case calibration, empirical risk-coverage, market-baseline and exact-score challenger evaluation.
summary.primaryRisk: Cron configuration on a preview branch is not evidence of scheduled execution because Vercel cron invocations target production deployments.

productionRuntime24h.note: The runtime status aggregation exposed no 5xx bucket in the current 24h query; this is not proof that every invocation was healthy.

runtimeWarning.interpretation: Transversal url.parse() deprecation warning remains unresolved; no direct ARGUS source call has yet been attributed, so do not patch blindly.

findings.observed: Vercel cron jobs invoke the production deployment URL. The research Control Plane cron is currently configured on a preview branch, so the planned 7-day/50+ scheduled-run experiment has not been proven to have started.
findings.derived: The current blocker is deployment scope, not model logic and not a cron failure.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Promote only the already-built zero-provider-call, zero-model-mutation Control Plane probe through the Maximum Pilot production safety gate after an authenticated manual endpoint/read-back validation; then observe one non-critical route prospectively.
findings.requiredEvidence: At least 7 prospective days and >=50 intended invocations; 100% lineage CONFIGURED->DEPLOYED->INVOKED->SUCCEEDED/FAILED->PERSISTED/NOT_PERSISTED; synthetic duplicate and overlap test; sampled cross-check against Vercel RequestId/invocation logs.
findings.failureCondition: Missing lineage, duplicate writes, lock suppresses legitimate runs, persistence read-back mismatch, or instrumentation changes provider/model behavior.
findings.rollback: Remove only the research cron/probe from production configuration; retain Watchtower and historical evidence.

findings.observed: Proper scores such as Brier and log-loss combine reliability/calibration, resolution and uncertainty; lower Brier alone does not prove better calibration. Reliability diagrams directly assess calibration.
findings.derived: ARGUS must evaluate ALL, ACCEPTED, PRIME, VALUE and NO_BET cohorts separately and pair proper scores with reliability bins/ECE and sample counts.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Keep selected-case-calibration read-only and report Brier, log-loss, ECE, reliability bins and sample size by decision cohort on frozen settled cases.
findings.requiredEvidence: >=200 settled accepted cases for directional reading, preference for >=500 for stronger conclusions, multiple forward temporal windows and no post-hoc recalibration of old decisions.
findings.failureCondition: Apparent improvement exists only globally, disappears in accepted cohorts, reliability worsens, or results reverse across forward windows.
findings.rollback: No production rollback required; endpoint is read-only/shadow.

findings.observed: Selective prediction literature formalizes coverage as the fraction accepted and selective risk as error on accepted predictions; stronger selectivity can reduce risk but does not guarantee monotonic improvement in every domain.
findings.derived: ARGUS should prove empirical risk-vs-coverage behavior before changing NO BET thresholds or importing conformal guarantees.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Continue the existing shadow risk-coverage curve across confidence/readiness thresholds and stratify later by league/market/window once sample size permits.
findings.requiredEvidence: Stable risk reduction as coverage falls across multiple independent forward windows, with confidence intervals/bootstrap by match and adequate samples per operating region.
findings.failureCondition: Risk curve is non-monotonic/unstable, selective gains vanish out-of-window, or coverage collapses without material risk improvement.
findings.rollback: Retain current NO BET policy; discard proposed threshold changes.
findings.candidateHypothesis: Formal conformal thresholding remains WATCH until football-specific exchangeability/drift assumptions are tested.

findings.observed: A 2026 preprint reports differences among multiplicative, Shin, Power and alternative odds-to-probability conversions on 90,014 football matches across five bookmakers, including favourite-longshot effects.
findings.derived: Simple proportional no-vig should not automatically be treated as market truth; ARGUS should compare de-margin methods on the same point-in-time settled cases.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Extend the existing proportional-vs-power audit offline only; add Shin/one-parameter favourite-longshot challenger only after odds provenance and bookmaker identity are complete.
findings.requiredEvidence: >=500 eligible point-in-time cases preferred, several bookmakers/leagues/windows, Brier/log-loss/reliability comparisons on identical cases.
findings.failureCondition: More complex conversion fails to improve proper scores consistently or gains depend on one bookmaker/window.
findings.rollback: Keep proportional no-vig as transparent baseline.
findings.reasonNotKeepYet: Primary 2026 result is a preprint and transfer to ARGUS data provenance is unvalidated.

findings.observed: Recent peer-reviewed football modelling work shows that independent Poisson assumptions can be too restrictive and that Dixon-Coles is one member of a broader dependence family; alternative dependence structures can fit leagues differently.
findings.derived: Exact-score R&D should benchmark simple models before any neural/LLM reranker: independent Poisson -> Dixon-Coles -> one dependence challenger.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Offline replay comparison using identical features and temporal splits; score the full scoreline distribution, not only top-1 exact-score accuracy.
findings.requiredEvidence: Several seasons/leagues with forward splits; full-distribution log-loss or ranked probability score, calibration/coherence with 1X2 and O/U, plus stability by league.
findings.failureCondition: Dependence challenger wins only in-sample, degrades 1X2/O-U coherence, or improvement is league-specific and unstable.
findings.rollback: Keep independent Poisson/Dixon-Coles baseline; no production effect.

findings.observed: A May 2026 preprint on 140 EPL matches reports that calibrating pre-match team strength to Betfair 1X2 and O/U prices was the dominant driver of in-play accuracy, with post-shot xG as a time-varying covariate.
findings.derived: Market anchoring is more plausible as a small shadow challenger than adding a large live architecture, but the published sample is too small for promotion.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Shadow-only replay using frozen pre-kickoff market probabilities plus only point-in-time event features proven available before each state.
findings.requiredEvidence: >=1000 independent matches preferred, multi-league, multiple forward windows, compare against both current ARGUS and market-only baseline; cluster uncertainty by match rather than live state.
findings.failureCondition: No gain over market-only baseline, gain disappears outside EPL/window, or event timestamps are incomplete/leaky.
findings.rollback: Discard challenger; preserve current live model.

findings.observed: API-SPORTS exposes daily and per-minute quota/remaining values in every response header. Pro is 7,500/day, 300/minute and 5/second; official guidance favors smoothing, cache and backoff.
findings.derived: ARGUS resource policy should treat provider headers as source-of-truth and increase data acquisition only when quota headroom and value-of-information justify it.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Capture quota headers from existing provider calls without adding requests, persist daily min/median remaining and tag 429/provider failures with current quota state.
findings.requiredEvidence: At least 3 UTC quota reset cycles and >=1000 existing provider responses; reconcile local counters to provider headers.
findings.failureCondition: Header capture materially alters request path, counters diverge persistently, or quota state cannot explain 429/provider failures.
findings.rollback: Disable instrumentation only; keep existing caching/polling policy.

findings.observed: Time-ordered validation is required to avoid training on future observations; TimeSeriesSplit explicitly supports a gap between train and test windows.
findings.derived: ARGUS walk-forward evaluation should document a temporal embargo/gap where feature availability or settlement latency could leak future information, rather than relying on chronology alone.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Audit existing walk-forward splits for feature cutoff and introduce a research-only configurable embargo in replay where same-day/near-kickoff feature availability is ambiguous.
findings.requiredEvidence: Zero feature timestamps after decision cutoff in sampled folds; results reported with and without embargo to reveal leakage sensitivity.
findings.failureCondition: Performance collapses under a realistic gap or any future-timestamp feature appears in training/decision state.
findings.rollback: No production mutation; retain stricter evaluation as truth source.

findings.observed: StatsBomb maintains official open football data with match, event, lineup and selected 360 files; repository data was updated in May 2026 and is intended for research use under stated attribution/terms.
findings.derived: It can support free offline experiments for event-state/xG-style feature engineering, but coverage does not match ARGUS production universe and must not be mixed with live evidence as if identical.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: Use a small documented subset offline to test event-timestamp handling and feature definitions, keeping a separate source/provenance namespace.
findings.requiredEvidence: License/attribution compliance, explicit competition coverage map, reproducible event ordering, no claim of production availability.
findings.failureCondition: Coverage mismatch creates non-transferable gains or feature cannot be reproduced from ARGUS production feeds.
findings.rollback: Remove the experimental dataset/challenger; no production dependency.

findings.observed: A July 2026 World Cup benchmark reports that four frontier LLM forecasting agents did not beat the betting market on Brier score across 104 matches, despite rich search/reflection loops.
findings.derived: ARGUS should not add an LLM exact-score/probability reranker merely for novelty. LLMs may remain useful for explanation, research synthesis or anomaly triage, not as an unvalidated probability engine.
findings.smallestSafeExperiment: None for primary forecasting. If used, restrict to read-only explanation/error taxonomy and never let text output overwrite calibrated probabilities.
findings.requiredEvidence: Would require independent, contamination-free, proper-score superiority over market/model baselines across large forward samples before reconsideration.
findings.failureCondition: Any probability degradation, calibration loss, non-reproducibility or narrative-driven confidence inflation.

rejectedWeakIdeas: Upgrade API-Football solely to accelerate learning without demonstrated quota bottleneck.
Promote conformal thresholds directly from non-football domains without drift/exchangeability validation.
Adopt published betting ROI as evidence of transferable edge.
Add a large live transformer before point-in-time event completeness and market-only baselines are proven.
Patch DEP0169 by guessing at application source before dependency attribution.

Instrument provider quota headers only on existing calls when code path is identified and validated.
Audit walk-forward feature cutoffs and add research embargo sensitivity test.

Do not use ROI alone as promotion criterion.
proofRequired: temporal leakage audit with realistic gap
